recommended: Retain Vadhan 2012 Open Problem 7.13: seed length O(n), with distinguishing security s(n)*(epsilon/m)^O(1) from the stated inversion hardness.
alternative: Fully black-box linear-seed construction at the same underlying input length, with standard asymptotic cryptographic security only.
reason: The merged 2024 black-box seed-exponent question is not equivalent to the original full quantitative security target.

recommended: Specialize to polynomial-factor GapSVP worst-case hardness, permitting a quantum security reduction; classical unbounded compact FHE, with no separate circular-security assumption.
alternative: Keep an arbitrary explicitly specified worst-case problem as part of the requested construction.

recommended: Hamming-distance input pairs: communication for a maximal-length algorithmic secret key, with complexity profile supplied and private randomness.
alternative: Hamming-distance input pairs: the full communication-versus-key-length tradeoff.
reason: Q17 asks about important examples without selecting a unique family or key-length target. The Hamming example is explicitly suggested in the source.

recommended: At least 2/3 of fair infinite random oracles, with logarithmic losses measured in the input lengths.
alternative: Almost surely over fair infinite random oracles, with the same logarithmic losses.
reason: The original question says for random X without choosing a probability quantifier; the finite-random-string theorem has a different size parameter.

recommended: Tensor-product perturbation H-prime with operator norm at most one.
alternative: General local H-prime with the baseline partition value supplied as input.
reason: The source does not specify an efficient representation of the additive perturbation or access to the starting value; zero-freeness alone does not supply a baseline computation.

recommended: One amplification step that doubles small normalized energy, preserves constraint arity, allows local-dimension growth and increases term count by a constant factor.
alternative: The stronger version also preserving a fixed local dimension.
reason: The source asks for all important features of the classical template without a quantitative target; preserving arity differs materially from preserving both arity and dimension.

recommended: Quantum error at most C*m*sqrt(epsilon), conditional entropy at least C*(k+log2(1/epsilon)), universal constant C.
alternative: Some polynomial loss in output length times a fixed positive power of classical error, with the stated entropy scaling.
reason: The primary excerpt leaves the allowed parameter deterioration unspecified; its cited operator-space source supplies the recommended quantitative question.

recommended: Polynomially many EPR pairs in input length, a constant-factor communication increase and constant additional error, for Boolean function computation.
alternative: Only O(log n) EPR pairs under the same communication and error conventions.
reason: The source asks for smaller entanglement without specifying an asymptotic resource bound; relations and state conversion have different known limitations.

recommended: Existence of an n*polylog(n)-bit randomized protocol for directed graphs with polynomially bounded integer capacities, constant error and locally decoded exact edge flows.
alternative: Determine the optimal communication complexity up to constant factors in that model.
reason: The source lists the near-linear threshold and the broader optimal-complexity target separately, without fixing which is the card objective.

recommended: A computable degree bound in n and the fixed polynomial sparsity exponent, allowing polynomial sparsity overhead.
alternative: The stronger degree bound 2^{poly(n)} with polynomial sparsity overhead.
reason: The source requests any degree bound; bare existence is finite-set trivial, and effective versus exponential bounds are different targets.

recommended: Optimal public-protocol success probability as a function of every player count k>=2, with absolute 1/100 accuracy.
alternative: Only the two-player optimal success probability, at the same accuracy.
reason: The source explicitly discusses both the two-player case and arbitrary numbers of players without selecting a single scope.

recommended: A fully explicit infinite family of unbounded graph sizes; every large integer size need not occur.
alternative: A fully explicit construction for every sufficiently large integer N.
reason: Section 4.3 uses infinite families and separately expresses a preference for dense sizes; Open Problem 4.43 leaves the size coverage unspecified.
